novelty.justification: The idea text only says existing tools 'work at the hunk level... or use language models at the function level but still omit essential vulnerability-relevant statements and lack robust verification mechanisms'; it does not specify any new technique beyond this problem statement.
novelty.rubric: Existing: the idea's core method is already clearly present or solved in the Solution Space; only tiny parameter / test-case changes.
novelty.differentiation: No concrete method is proposed; the artifact restates the task background and evaluation setup rather than introducing a new porting mechanism.

feasibility.justification: The artifact describes constructing a CVE-based C patch porting dataset via 'collecting CVE patches from NVD/GitHub' and 'manually filter to function-level changes', which is a heavy, multi-step engineering effort; however, no actual system or algorithm is specified to evaluate feasibility.
feasibility.rubric: Extreme engineering barrier: requires building complex low-level tooling from scratch (custom compiler plugins, new vulnerability execution sandboxes), or an extremely heavy experimental pipeline with multi-month development.

clarity.justification: The text provides a clear problem and experiment setup ('Fine-tuning set: 2,842 CVEs... Evaluation set: 694 CVEs...') but never states the proposed solution or how patches would be generated, so the logic from problem to method is missing.
clarity.rubric: Broken logic: states a problem but the proposed solution does not match it, or never mentions experiments / evaluation.

Without a technical contribution, novelty is absent relative to existing backporting/transplantation work, and clarity/feasibility cannot be meaningfully assessed. It needs a specific mechanism before it can be scored as a viable idea.

original.overall_conclusion: Mystique, an LLM-based patch porting approach with semantic/syntactic signature extraction and iterative checking-refining, achieves 0.954 function-level and 0.924 CVE-level success, outperforming TSBPORT by 13.2% and 12.3% respectively. It also demonstrates better generality across LLMs, projects, bugs, and Java, and successfully ports 34 real-world vulnerable branches.
original.comparable_notes: Fair comparison should use the same 694 CVE / 1,359 function patch porting dataset and the same fine-tuning split (pre/post CodeLlama release date). PPatHF was fine-tuned on a larger commit-history dataset (23,561 Linux + 7,913 other commits) rather than the same patch porting task. FixMorph was evaluated only on Linux subset due to compilation constraints. Metrics include Exact Match, Success (semantic equivalence), Failure rate, and Code BLEU; success is based on semantic equivalence to manually ported patches.
